messages:
zoe (support): customer: invoice for April shows 12,180 billed tokens but their dashboard session shows ~6.1k served tokens. raised as billing escalation. assigning triage. attaching excerpt and repro notes.

maya (support): ack. can you paste sample request/response + any request_id and region?

zoe (support): here's one pair: request_id=cust-9a3, region=us-west-2, model=rwd-open-30b, time=2026-02-12T14:03Z

zoe (support): curl we used to repro:```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-open-30b","input":"Summarize: <long prefix>","stream":false}'
```

zoe (support): runtime logs for that request (redacted):```
[14:03:01.123] request_id=cust-9a3 batch_id=842 stage=batching queued
[14:03:01.128] batch_id=842 merge_count=5 shared_prefix_hash=0x7a12 prefetch_hit=true
[14:03:01.130] model_compute_tokens=410 served_tokens=210 meter_emitted_tokens=820
[14:03:01.131] response_sent request_id=cust-9a3 status=200
```

kevin (infra): wow meter_emitted_tokens=820 vs served_tokens=210 looks like double/multiplying. that merge_count=5 + prefetch_hit=true is suspicious.

maya (support): customer claims many of their calls are identical prefix-batched, they use continuous batching heavily. could merge_count explain invoice > dashboard?

ryan (ops): short answer: yes. current metering path increments the per-request token counter before we apply prefix dedup for KV cache hits when a batch contains multiple requests sharing the same prefix. so when the batch merges 5 requests that all share a cached prefix, model did compute once (model_compute_tokens=410) but we incorrectly emitted token counts per original requests leading to ~5x counting for metering.

alyssa (billing): that would inflate invoices. do we have scope (how many invoices affected)?

kevin (infra): preliminary query over April shows a ~0.7% spike in metered tokens in accounts with continuous-batching usage pattern. I have a script but need a confirm window to run full backfill.

kevin (infra): repro note: the bug lives in the meter-emitter hook that runs when batch is accepted. it currently multiplies by batch.request_count instead of deduping by shared_prefix_key when prefetch_hit=true.

zoe (support): customer wants to know if we will credit the overage. pls advise temporary mitigation and ETA for fix.

maya (support): workaround: ask customers to disable continuous batching or set their routing to not merge identical prefixes. not ideal. any shorter workaround?

ryan (ops): short-term mitigation we can do server-side: flip metering hook to use per-batch unique-prefix dedup until patch ships. that's a config toggle; low risk. I'll prepare a canary.

kevin (infra): I can prepare a hotfix to ensure meter_emitted_tokens = sum(unique(model_contribution_by_prefix)) rather than sum(per-request). patch ready, running unit + integration.

metering-bot: canary plan created: metering-dedup-toggle -> canary in us-west-2 (10% traffic) -> monitor token delta and latency for 6 hours.

alyssa (billing): if canary proves stable, we'll run a scoped credit for affected invoices where the delta > 5% and where continuous-batching was used. need list of request_ids/accounts.

kevin (infra): tests pass locally, deploying canary now. tagging release: infra/metering/fix-dup-190345.

ryan (ops): rolling canary at 14:50Z. monitor query:```sql
-- quick aggregation
select account_id, sum(metered_tokens) as billed, sum(served_tokens) as served, count(*)
from token_events
where date >= '2026-04-01' and continuous_batching = true
group by account_id
order by billed-served desc
limit 20;
```

kevin (infra): canary showed expected effect: for sample batch_id=842 above, post-fix logs:```
[14:55:01.130] batch_id=842 merge_count=5 shared_prefix_hash=0x7a12 prefetch_hit=true
[14:55:01.131] model_compute_tokens=410 served_tokens=210 meter_emitted_tokens=410
```

kevin (infra): note meter_emitted_tokens now matches model compute (410) not multiplied by merge_count.

maya (support): thanks. what's timeline to flip globally and backfill?

kevin (infra): if canary stays green for 6h, we'll promote to 100% over 2h. backfill: we can run a one-off reprocess job to recompute metered_events for April for affected accounts; estimate 12-18h job and then a billing reconciliation.

alyssa (billing): ok prepare a customer communication: we will credit the overbilled delta for accounts where recomputed_metered < invoiced by >5% and continuous-batching usage confirmed. Billing will need list of invoices and amounts.

zoe (support): I'll draft the customer note and wait for final numbers. pls add me to the backfill status channel.

ryan (ops): added. I'll post periodic progress and ETA updates.

kevin (infra): action items: 1) promote fix 2) execute backfill recompute job 3) generate delta report per account 4) coordinate credits with billing.

maya (support): tagging customer with interim note: "we identified a metering duplication bug related to continuous batching + prefix caching. we're rolling a fix and will reconcile invoices. Apologies for the trouble." :pray:  

zoe (support): customer replied: "thanks, appreciate the quick triage — please circle back once credits are posted."

metering-bot: canary metrics after 6h: token-delta drop in canary accounts = 98th percentile -72% on duplicated events, no latency regression.

kevin (infra): promoting to 100% now.

zoe (support): closing loop once backfill and credits complete. leaving thread open for billing finalization. :white_check_mark:
